level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang TAMA ayon kay Section 400 ng CMTA tungkol sa pagpasok ng mga imported goods?

choices.A: Maaari lang ipasok ang mga imported goods sa Pilipinas sa pamamagitan ng anumang paliparan o daungan, kahit walang customs office.
choices.B: Ang mga imported goods ay hindi na kailangang dumaan sa customs kung ang halaga ay mababa sa P10,000.
choices.C: Ang free zone ay hindi maaaring gamitin bilang paraan ng pag-admit ng goods.
choices.D: Lahat ng imported goods ay dapat i-enter sa isang customs office sa isang port of entry, o puwedeng tanggapin o alisin mula sa isang free zone.

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: D. Ayon sa Section 400, 'All goods imported into the Philippines shall be entered through a customs office at a port of entry, or may be admitted to or removed from a free zone as defined in this Act, as the case may be.' Mahalagang tandaan na ang free zone ay isa ring legal na paraan ng pagpasok ng goods, kaya mali ang mga choice na nagsasabing bawal ito o dapat palaging dumaan sa regular na customs office.

level2.question: Under Section 400 of the CMTA, through what must all goods imported into the Philippines be entered?

choices.A: A customs office at a port of entry, or admitted to/removed from a free zone
choices.B: Any airport regardless of registration
choices.C: A Bureau of Internal Revenue office
choices.D: A local government unit only

level2.reason: Correct answer: A. Section 400 of the CMTA states that 'All goods imported into the Philippines shall be entered through a customs office at a port of entry, or may be admitted to or removed from a free zone as defined in this Act, as the case may be.' This confirms that both a formal customs office and a free zone are valid channels for importation, ruling out any option that excludes free zones or names an unrelated agency.

180._title: Title IV – Import Clearance and Formalities

level1.question: Ayon sa Section 401, alin sa mga sumusunod ang HINDI kabilang sa mga uri ng goods declaration na nakasaad sa CMTA?

choices.A: For re-exportation
choices.B: For consumption
choices.D: For customs transit

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 401, 'A goods declaration may be for consumption, for customs bonded warehousing, for admission, for conditional importation, or for customs transit.' Ang re-exportation ay hindi kabilang sa limang uri ng goods declaration na binanggit dito kaya ito ang tamang sagot sa tanong.

level2.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the types of goods declaration listed under Section 401 of the CMTA?

choices.A: For consumption
choices.B: For customs bonded warehousing
choices.D: For customs transit

level2.reason: Correct answer: C. Section 401 states that 'A goods declaration may be for consumption, for customs bonded warehousing, for admission, for conditional importation, or for customs transit.' Re-exportation is not among these five categories, making it the correct exception to identify.

182._title: Title IV – Import Clearance and Formalities

level1.question: Ang mga goods na may FOB o FCA value na mas mababa sa P50,000 ay dumadaan sa informal entry process ayon sa Section 402. Tama o Mali?

choices.A: False
choices.B: Cannot be Determined
choices.D: Partially True

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: C. Ayon sa Section 402(a), kasama sa informal entry ang 'Goods of a commercial nature with Free on Board (FOB) or Free Carrier At (FCA) value of less than fifty thousand pesos (P50,000.00).' Ito ay isa sa mga pinaka-testable na threshold sa CMTA kaya dapat itong ikumpara sa P10,000 de minimis value para hindi malito.

level2.question: Under Section 402(a), goods of a commercial nature qualify for informal entry if their FOB or FCA value is:

choices.A: Exactly P50,000
choices.B: P100,000 or below
choices.D: Less than P50,000

level2.reason: Correct answer: D. Section 402(a) covers 'Goods of a commercial nature with Free on Board (FOB) or Free Carrier At (FCA) value of less than fifty thousand pesos (P50,000.00)' for informal entry processing. Note the threshold is strictly less than P50,000, not equal to or above it, and this figure is adjusted every three years using the CPI.

184._title: Title IV – Import Clearance and Formalities

level1.question: Ilang araw ang ibinibigay sa declarant para kumpletuhin ang impormasyon o dokumento matapos maghain ng provisional goods declaration ayon sa Section 403?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.D: 45 days

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: D. Ayon sa Section 403, dapat 'complete the information or submit the supporting documents within forty-five (45) days from the filing of the provisional goods declaration.' Maaari pa itong i-extend ng Bureau ng karagdagang 45 days kung may valid na dahilan, kaya huwag ikumpara ito sa 15-day period ng regular na goods declaration.

level2.question: Under Section 403, how long may the Bureau extend the period to complete a provisional goods declaration beyond the initial 45 days?

choices.A: 15 days
choices.B: 30 days
choices.D: 60 days

level2.reason: Correct answer: C. Section 403 provides that the initial 45-day period 'may be extended by the Bureau for another forty-five (45) days for valid reasons.' This means the total possible period for completing a provisional goods declaration can reach 90 days if the extension is granted.

185._title: Title IV – Import Clearance and Formalities

level1.question: Sino ang itinuturing na may-ari ng imported goods ayon sa Section 404 ng CMTA?

choices.A: Ang shipping line lamang
choices.B: Ang consignee o holder ng bill of lading, airway bill, o katumbas na transport document
choices.D: Ang broker na humahawak ng dokumento

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 404, 'All goods imported into the Philippines shall be deemed to be the property of the consignee or the holder of the bill of lading, airway bill or other equivalent transport document.' Kasama rin sa depinisyon ang underwriters ng abandoned goods at salvors ng goods mula sa wreck.

level2.question: Under Section 404, imported goods are deemed to be the property of:

choices.A: The freight forwarder only
choices.B: The consignee or the holder of the bill of lading, airway bill, or other equivalent transport document
choices.D: The shipping line

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 404 states that 'All goods imported into the Philippines shall be deemed to be the property of the consignee or the holder of the bill of lading, airway bill or other equivalent transport document.' The provision also extends ownership recognition to underwriters of abandoned goods and salvors in wreck situations.

186._title: Title IV – Import Clearance and Formalities

level1.question: Ang liability ng importer para sa duties at taxes ay personal debt lamang at hindi maaaring maging lien sa goods ayon sa Section 405. Tama o Mali?

choices.A: False
choices.B: Partially True
choices.D: True

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 405, ang liability ng importer ay 'constitutes a personal debt due and demandable against the importer' at sabay-sabay ring 'It also constitutes a lien on the imported goods which may be enforced while such goods are under customs' custody.' Mali ang sinasabi ng tanong dahil hindi lang ito personal debt, ito rin ay lien sa goods.

level2.question: Under Section 405, the liability for duties and taxes attached to importation is best described as:

choices.A: A personal debt only, with no lien on the goods
choices.B: A lien on the goods only, not a personal debt
choices.C: Neither a personal debt nor a lien
choices.D: Both a personal debt and a lien on the imported goods

level2.reason: Correct answer: D. Section 405 provides that the importer's liability 'constitutes a personal debt due and demandable against the importer' and 'also constitutes a lien on the imported goods which may be enforced while such goods are under customs' custody.' The law establishes both forms of liability simultaneously, not one to the exclusion of the other.

level2.question: Under Section 407, within how many days from the discharge of the last package must the goods declaration be lodged?

choices.A: 30 days

level1.question: Kailan dapat matanggap ang request para amyendahan ang isang goods declaration na naihain na, ayon sa Section 408?

choices.A: Anumang oras kahit pagkatapos ng final assessment
choices.B: Bago dumating ang goods sa Pilipinas
choices.C: Sa loob ng 3 taon mula sa paghain
choices.D: Bago ang final assessment o examination ng goods

level2.question: Under Section 408, a request to amend a lodged goods declaration must be received:

choices.A: Anytime within 3 years
choices.B: After final assessment
choices.C: Prior to final assessment or examination of the goods
choices.D: Within 15 days of arrival

level2.reason: Correct answer: C. Section 408 requires that a request to amend a lodged goods declaration 'must be received prior to final assessment or examination of the goods.' Once assessment or examination has been completed, amendments are no longer permitted under this provision.

level1.question: Ayon sa Section 101 ng CMTA, ano ang isa sa mga layunin ng Estado?

choices.A: Hadlangan ang international trade
choices.B: Efficiently facilitate international trade
choices.D: Palakasin lamang ang mga smuggler

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 101, layunin ng Estado na 'efficiently facilitate international trade, prevent and curtail any form of customs fraud and illegal acts, and modernize customs and tariff administration.' Mali ang choice A dahil kabaligtaran ito ng layunin ng batas na padaliin, hindi hadlangan, ang legitimate trade.

level2.question: Under Section 101 of the CMTA, the Declaration of Policy states that the State shall institute customs and tariff management that will:

choices.A: Restrict all forms of international trade
choices.B: Efficiently facilitate international trade
choices.D: Prioritize revenue over trade facilitation exclusively

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 101 states that the State shall institute 'fair and transparent customs and tariff management that will efficiently facilitate international trade, prevent and curtail any form of customs fraud and illegal acts.' The provision balances trade facilitation with revenue protection and fraud prevention, not one at the expense of the other.

level3.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between trade facilitation and fraud prevention under Section 101's Declaration of Policy?

choices.A: Trade facilitation is prioritized exclusively, and fraud prevention is secondary
choices.B: Fraud prevention takes precedence, and trade facilitation is discouraged
choices.C: Both are pursued simultaneously as complementary State policies
choices.D: The CMTA does not address fraud prevention as a policy goal

level3.reason: Correct answer: C. Section 101 declares the State's policy to institute customs management that will 'efficiently facilitate international trade, prevent and curtail any form of customs fraud and illegal acts, and modernize customs and tariff administration.' The provision treats facilitation and fraud control as twin, coexisting goals rather than competing priorities, which is a common conceptual trap in board exam questions.

level4.question: A customs broker at the Port of Manila argues that strict document verification requirements violate the CMTA's policy of trade facilitation. Based on Section 101, is this argument correct?

choices.A: Yes, because trade facilitation means eliminating all verification steps
choices.B: No, because the CMTA also declares a policy to prevent and curtail customs fraud, so reasonable verification is consistent with the law
choices.C: Yes, because the CMTA prohibits any form of documentary requirement
choices.D: No, because trade facilitation is not mentioned in the CMTA

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 101 states the State's policy is to 'efficiently facilitate international trade, prevent and curtail any form of customs fraud and illegal acts,' showing that facilitation and fraud control operate together. Reasonable verification measures serve the fraud-prevention half of this dual policy and do not contradict trade facilitation.

level5.question: What CMTA section contains the Declaration of Policy that includes both trade facilitation and fraud prevention as State objectives?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Section 101. This section of the CMTA states the State's policy to 'efficiently facilitate international trade, prevent and curtail any form of customs fraud and illegal acts, and modernize customs and tariff administration.' It is the foundational policy provision that frames the rest of the Act's objectives.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa pagbabawas o pag-alis, sa kabuuan o bahagi, ng duties and taxes kung saan hindi pa nababayaran ang mga ito?

choices.A: Refund
choices.B: Abatement
choices.D: Drawback

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(a), ang Abatement ay 'the reduction or diminution, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes where payment has not been made.' Mahalagang tandaan na ito ay bago pa mabayaran ang duties, samantalang ang Refund ay pagkatapos nang nabayaran na.

level2.question: Under Section 102(a) of the CMTA, 'Abatement' refers to:

choices.A: The return of duties and taxes already paid
choices.B: The reduction or diminution, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes where payment has not been made
choices.C: The exemption of relief consignments from duties
choices.D: The temporary release of goods pending dispute resolution

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(a) defines Abatement as 'the reduction or diminution, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes where payment has not been made.' This distinguishes it from Refund, which applies to duties and taxes already paid.

level3.question: What is the key distinction between Abatement and Refund under the CMTA?

choices.A: Abatement applies before payment; Refund applies after payment has been made
choices.B: Abatement applies only to exported goods; Refund applies only to imported goods
choices.C: Abatement and Refund are identical concepts under the CMTA
choices.D: Abatement requires court approval; Refund does not

level3.reason: Correct answer: A. Section 102(a) defines Abatement as a reduction of duties and taxes 'where payment has not been made,' while Section 102(ll) defines Refund as the return of duties and taxes 'paid on goods.' The timing of payment relative to the reduction or return is the critical distinguishing factor frequently tested in CuBLE.

level4.question: An importer at the Port of Cebu discovers, before paying any duties, that the assessed amount is excessive due to a computation error. What remedy under the CMTA definitions would apply to reduce the amount owed before payment?

choices.A: Refund
choices.B: Abatement
choices.D: Reexportation

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Since Section 102(a) defines Abatement as 'the reduction or diminution, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes where payment has not been made,' this is the applicable remedy when the correction happens before payment. Refund would only apply if the importer had already paid the excessive amount.

level5.question: What CMTA term refers to the reduction or diminution of duties and taxes where payment has not yet been made?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Abatement. Section 102(a) of the CMTA defines it as 'the reduction or diminution, in whole or in part, of duties and taxes where payment has not been made.' It is distinguished from Refund, which involves duties already paid.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa pagpasok ng imported goods, direkta man o sa pamamagitan ng transit, patungo sa isang free zone?

choices.A: Entry
choices.B: Admission
choices.D: Lodgement

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(c), ang Admission ay ang 'act of bringing imported goods directly or through transit into a free zone.' Iba ito sa Entry, na tumutukoy sa pagpasok ng goods sa customs territory.

level2.question: Under Section 102(c) of the CMTA, 'Admission' refers to:

choices.A: The act of bringing imported goods into the customs territory
choices.B: The act of bringing imported goods directly or through transit into a free zone
choices.C: The completion of formalities allowing goods to be exported
choices.D: The registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(c) defines Admission as 'the act of bringing imported goods directly or through transit into a free zone.' It is distinct from Entry, which under Section 102(r) applies to goods brought into the customs territory.

level3.question: How is 'Admission' distinguished from 'Entry' under the CMTA?

choices.A: Admission applies to goods brought into a free zone, while Entry applies to goods brought into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones
choices.B: Admission and Entry are interchangeable terms
choices.C: Admission applies only to exported goods
choices.D: Entry applies exclusively to relief consignments

level3.reason: Correct answer: A. Section 102(c) defines Admission as bringing goods 'into a free zone,' while Section 102(r) defines Entry as bringing goods 'into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones.' This distinction, based on destination, is a favorite CuBLE comparison question.

level4.question: A shipment of raw materials arrives at the Port of Subic and is brought directly into the Subic Bay Freeport Zone without entering the customs territory. What CMTA term applies to this movement?

choices.A: Entry
choices.B: Admission
choices.D: Transshipment

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Since the goods are brought 'directly or through transit into a free zone' such as the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, this matches the Section 102(c) definition of Admission. Entry would instead apply if the goods moved into the customs territory.

level5.question: What CMTA term describes bringing imported goods directly or through transit into a free zone?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Admission. Section 102(c) of the CMTA defines it as 'the act of bringing imported goods directly or through transit into a free zone.' It is commonly contrasted with Entry, which covers movement into the customs territory.

level1.question: Ano ang AEO ayon sa CMTA?

choices.A: Isang uri ng smuggling
choices.B: Isang entity na duly accredited ng Bureau batay sa WCO Framework of Standards
choices.D: Isang uri ng free zone

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(g), ang AEO ay tumutukoy sa entity na 'duly accredited by the Bureau based on the World Customs Organization (WCO) Framework of Standards to Secure and Facilitate Global Trade.' Layunin nito ang trade facilitation sa pamamagitan ng risk management.

level2.question: Under Section 102(g), the accreditation of an Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) is based primarily on:

choices.A: The Intellectual Property Code
choices.B: The WCO Framework of Standards to Secure and Facilitate Global Trade, the RKC, and WCO Supply Chain Management Guidelines
choices.D: The Customs Brokers Act of 2004

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(g) states that AEO accreditation is based on 'the World Customs Organization (WCO) Framework of Standards to Secure and Facilitate Global Trade, the Revised Kyoto Convention (RKC), the WCO Supply Chain Management Guidelines and the various national best practices.' This international basis is a commonly tested detail distinguishing AEO from purely domestic accreditation schemes.

level3.question: What is the primary purpose of the AEO program as reflected in its CMTA definition?

choices.A: To restrict the number of importers allowed to operate
choices.B: To promote trade facilitation and seamless movement of goods through secure supply chains using risk management and modern technology
choices.C: To eliminate the need for customs brokers
choices.D: To impose additional tariffs on accredited entities

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(g) states that AEO accreditation aims 'to promote trade facilitation and to provide a seamless movement of goods across borders through secure international trade supply chains with the use of risk management and modern technology.' This links AEO status to facilitation benefits rather than added restrictions, a key concept for CuBLE.

level4.question: A freight forwarder operating at the Clark Freeport Zone seeks Bureau accreditation to receive facilitation benefits based on international supply-chain security standards. What CMTA-defined status is the forwarder pursuing?

choices.A: Declarant
choices.B: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO)
choices.D: Carrier

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(g) defines an AEO as including forwarders and freight forwarders 'duly accredited by the Bureau' based on international frameworks like the WCO Framework of Standards, aimed at facilitating trade through secure supply chains. This matches the forwarder's pursuit of accreditation-based facilitation benefits.

level5.question: What CMTA-defined status is granted to importers, exporters, customs brokers, and other entities accredited by the Bureau based on WCO international standards to facilitate secure trade?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO). Section 102(g) defines it as an entity 'duly accredited by the Bureau based on the World Customs Organization (WCO) Framework of Standards to Secure and Facilitate Global Trade.' AEO is a frequently tested board-exam topic tied to trade facilitation and risk management.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang bibigyan ng prayoridad sa examination ayon kay Section 419?

choices.A: Live animals at perishable goods
choices.B: Mga de-kahong gamit sa bahay
choices.D: Mga libro at dokumento

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 419, 'Priority in the examination shall be given to live animals, perishable goods and other goods requiring immediate examination.' Layunin nito na maiwasan ang pagkasira o pagkamatay ng mga produktong ito habang naghihintay ng inspeksyon.

level2.question: Under Section 419, which goods are given priority in examination?

choices.A: Live animals, perishable goods, and other goods requiring immediate examination
choices.B: Machinery and equipment
choices.D: Textiles and garments

level2.reason: Correct answer: A. Section 419 states that 'Priority in the examination shall be given to live animals, perishable goods and other goods requiring immediate examination.' This priority exists to prevent spoilage, loss, or harm to goods that are especially time-sensitive.

level3.question: Which government office is referred to as the 'Commission' as distinguished from the 'Bureau' under Section 102 of the CMTA?

choices.A: Department of Finance
choices.B: Tariff Commission
choices.D: Securities and Exchange Commission

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(l) defines 'Commission' as referring to the Tariff Commission, while Section 102(i) defines 'Bureau' as the Bureau of Customs. Distinguishing these two closely related terms is a common trap in CuBLE terminology questions.

level4.question: A District Collector at the Port of Batangas issues an order enforcing a CMTA provision. Under Section 102(i), what agency does the 'Bureau' refer to in this context?

choices.A: Department of Finance
choices.B: Bureau of Customs
choices.D: Tariff Commission

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(i) defines the 'Bureau' as the 'Bureau of Customs,' the agency responsible for enforcing customs laws through its District Collectors and other officers.

level5.question: Under Section 102(i) of the CMTA, what does the term 'Bureau' refer to?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Bureau of Customs. Section 102(i) of the CMTA states that 'Bureau refers to the Bureau of Customs.' It is distinct from the 'Commission,' which refers to the Tariff Commission.

level1.question: Alin sa sumusunod ang halimbawa ng nonintrusive examination na maaaring gamitin ng Bureau of Customs ayon sa Section 420?

choices.B: Manual na pagbilang ng mga item
choices.D: Pagtanggal ng packaging

level2.question: Under Section 420, which of the following exemplifies a nonintrusive method of examination that the Bureau may adopt?

choices.A: Use of x-ray machines
choices.B: Manual unpacking of all cargo
choices.D: Random opening of containers

This method allows inspection without physically opening every package, unlike the other options listed.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa pagkumpleto ng customs at ibang government formalities para makapasok ang goods for consumption, warehousing, transit, o transshipment, o para maexport?

choices.A: Lodgement
choices.B: Clearance
choices.D: Admission

Ito ang huling hakbang bago makalabas o makapasok ang goods.

level2.question: Under Section 102(k), 'Clearance' refers to:

choices.A: The registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau
choices.B: The completion of customs and other government formalities necessary to allow goods to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit or transshipment, or to be exported or placed under another customs procedure
choices.C: The reduction of duties and taxes before payment
choices.D: The physical inspection of goods for smuggling

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(k) defines Clearance precisely as the completion of formalities that allow goods 'to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit or transshipment, or to be exported or placed under another customs procedure.' It covers both import and export processes.

level3.question: Which of the following best captures the scope of 'Clearance' under Section 102(k) of the CMTA?

choices.A: It applies only to goods for consumption
choices.B: It applies broadly to formalities enabling entry for consumption, warehousing, transit, transshipment, export, or other customs procedures

choices.D: It refers solely to payment of duties and taxes

Section 102(k) broadly defines Clearance to cover formalities for goods 'to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit or transshipment, or to be exported or placed under another customs procedure.' Its broad scope, covering both import and export procedures, is a key distinction from narrower terms like Entry or Admission.

level4.question: A shipment at the Port of Davao completes all customs and government formalities, allowing it to be released for warehousing. What CMTA term describes this completed process?

choices.A: Lodgement
choices.B: Clearance
choices.D: Assessment

Section 102(k) defines Clearance as the 'completion of customs and other government formalities necessary to allow goods to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit or transshipment.' Completing all formalities for warehousing release matches this definition exactly.

level5.question: What CMTA term refers to the completion of customs and other government formalities necessary to allow goods to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit, transshipment, or export?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Clearance. Section 102(k) of the CMTA defines it as the 'completion of customs and other government formalities necessary to allow goods to enter for consumption, warehousing, transit or transshipment, or to be exported or placed under another customs procedure.'

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa customs procedure kung saan pwedeng dalhin ang goods sa customs territory nang may conditional relief mula sa duties and taxes, dahil layunin itong i-reexport sa loob ng specified period?

choices.A: Reexportation
choices.B: Conditional Importation
choices.D: Free Importation

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(m), ang Conditional Importation, na tinatawag ding temporary admission sa ilalim ng RKC, ay para sa goods na 'imported for a specific purpose and must be intended for reexportation within a specified period.' Dapat walang substantial change ang goods maliban sa normal depreciation.

level2.question: Under Section 102(m), Conditional Importation is known under the Revised Kyoto Convention (RKC) as:

choices.A: Free circulation
choices.B: Temporary admission
choices.D: Permanent entry

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(m) states that Conditional Importation 'refers to the customs procedure known under the RKC as temporary admission.' Goods under this procedure are conditionally relieved, totally or partially, from import duties and taxes.

level3.question: Which requirement is essential for goods to qualify as Conditional Importation under Section 102(m)?

choices.A: The goods must be permanently sold within the customs territory
choices.B: The goods must be intended for reexportation within a specified period without substantial change, except normal depreciation
choices.C: The goods must be manufactured domestically
choices.D: The goods must be exempt from all future duties regardless of use

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(m) requires that goods under Conditional Importation 'be imported for a specific purpose and must be intended for reexportation within a specified period and without having undergone any substantial change except due to normal depreciation.' This reexportation requirement is the defining feature tested on board exams.

level4.question: A foreign film production company brings specialized camera equipment into the Port of Manila for a three-month shoot, intending to bring the equipment back out of the country afterward with only normal wear. What CMTA procedure applies?

choices.A: Reexportation
choices.B: Conditional Importation
choices.D: Free Importation

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Since the equipment is 'imported for a specific purpose' and 'intended for reexportation within a specified period' without substantial change beyond normal depreciation, Section 102(m) classifies this as Conditional Importation, also known as temporary admission under the RKC.

level5.question: What CMTA term, known under the RKC as temporary admission, refers to goods conditionally relieved from duties and taxes because they are intended for reexportation within a specified period?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Conditional Importation. Section 102(m) of the CMTA defines it as goods 'conditionally relieved, totally or partially, from payment of import duties and taxes' that 'must be intended for reexportation within a specified period.' It is known under the RKC as temporary admission.

level1.question: Sino ang tinatawag na Customs Broker ayon sa CMTA?

choices.A: Sinumang may valid Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card mula sa PRC batay sa RA 9280
choices.B: Sinumang empleyado ng Bureau of Customs
choices.D: Sinumang freight forwarder

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 102(n), ang Customs Broker ay 'bona fide holder of a valid Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card issued by the Professional Regulatory Board and Professional Regulation Commission pursuant to Republic Act No. 9280.' Ang RA 9280 ay kilala bilang Customs Brokers Act of 2004.

level2.question: Under Section 102(n) of the CMTA, a Customs Broker must be a bona fide holder of a valid Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card issued pursuant to:

choices.A: Republic Act No. 7916
choices.B: Republic Act No. 9280
choices.D: Republic Act No. 7227

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(n) states that the Customs Broker's certificate is 'issued by the Professional Regulatory Board and Professional Regulation Commission pursuant to Republic Act No. 9280, as amended.' This law is otherwise known as the Customs Brokers Act of 2004, and its specific number is a frequently tested detail.

level3.question: Under Section 107, how does the liability of a licensed customs broker differ from that of the declarant regarding payment of duties and taxes?

choices.A: Both are equally liable for payment of duties and taxes
choices.B: The customs broker is responsible for the accuracy of the goods declaration but not for payment of duties, taxes and other charges, while the declarant is responsible for both
choices.C: Only the customs broker is liable for payment
choices.D: Neither is liable for payment or accuracy

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 107 states the declarant is responsible for accuracy and for payment of duties, taxes and other charges, while 'the licensed customs broker shall likewise be responsible for the accuracy of the goods declaration but shall not be responsible for the payment of duties, taxes and other charges.' This distinction between accuracy liability and payment liability is a classic CuBLE analytical question.

level4.question: A licensed customs broker at the Port of Iloilo signs a goods declaration but the importer fails to pay the assessed duties. Under Section 107, is the customs broker liable for the unpaid duties?

choices.A: Yes, the broker is solidarily liable for all duties and taxes
choices.B: No, the broker is responsible for the accuracy of the declaration but not for payment of duties, taxes and other charges
choices.C: Yes, but only up to 50% of the amount
choices.D: No, because brokers have no responsibilities under the CMTA

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 107 clarifies that while the declarant is responsible for payment of duties, taxes and other charges, 'the licensed customs broker shall likewise be responsible for the accuracy of the goods declaration but shall not be responsible for the payment of duties, taxes and other charges due on the imported goods.'

level5.question: Under what Republic Act is a person recognized as a Customs Broker required to hold a Certificate of Registration/Professional Identification Card, as cited in Section 102(n) of the CMTA?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Republic Act No. 9280. Section 102(n) of the CMTA states that the certificate is issued 'pursuant to Republic Act No. 9280, as amended.' This law is informally known as the Customs Brokers Act of 2004 and governs the licensing of customs brokers in the Philippines.

level1.question: Ano ang Entry ayon sa Section 102(r) ng CMTA?

choices.A: Ang act, documentation at process ng pagdadala ng imported goods sa customs territory, kasama ang goods na galing sa free zones
choices.B: Ang pagbabawas ng duties bago mabayaran
choices.C: Ang pagdadala ng goods papasok sa isang free zone
choices.D: Ang pag-export ng goods palabas ng bansa

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 102(r), ang Entry ay tumutukoy sa 'act, documentation and process of bringing imported goods into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones.' Iba ito sa Admission, na tungkol sa pagpasok papuntang free zone.

level2.question: Under Section 102(r), 'Entry' includes goods coming from:

choices.A: Only foreign countries directly
choices.B: Free zones
choices.D: Only relief consignment sources

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(r) defines Entry as bringing imported goods into the customs territory, 'including goods coming from free zones.' This shows that Entry applies not only to goods arriving directly from abroad but also to those transferred from free zones.

level3.question: Which statement correctly compares Entry and Admission under Section 102 of the CMTA?

choices.A: Entry is for free zones; Admission is for the customs territory
choices.B: Entry is for the customs territory, including goods from free zones; Admission is for bringing goods into a free zone
choices.C: Entry and Admission both apply exclusively to exported goods
choices.D: There is no meaningful distinction between the two terms

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(r) defines Entry as bringing goods 'into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones,' while Section 102(c) defines Admission as bringing goods 'into a free zone.' This directional distinction is a classic CuBLE comparison question.

level4.question: Goods previously admitted into the PEZA-registered Cavite Economic Zone are later moved into the Philippine customs territory for local sale. What CMTA term applies to this movement?

choices.A: Admission
choices.B: Entry
choices.D: Reexportation

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(r) defines Entry as bringing imported goods 'into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones.' Since the goods move from the free zone into the customs territory, this movement is classified as Entry.

level5.question: What CMTA term refers to the act, documentation, and process of bringing imported goods into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Entry. Section 102(r) of the CMTA defines it as 'the act, documentation and process of bringing imported goods into the customs territory, including goods coming from free zones.' It is distinguished from Admission, which applies to movement into a free zone.

level1.question: Ano ang Exportation ayon sa CMTA?

choices.A: Pagpasok ng goods sa Pilipinas
choices.B: Act, documentation, at process ng pagdadala ng goods palabas ng Philippine territory
choices.D: Pagbabayad ng duties

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(s), ang Exportation ay 'the act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory.' Ito ang kabaligtaran ng Importation.

level2.question: Under Section 102(s) of the CMTA, 'Exportation' refers to:

choices.A: The act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory
choices.B: The act of bringing goods into a free zone
choices.C: The reexportation of previously imported goods
choices.D: The registration of a goods declaration

level2.reason: Correct answer: A. Section 102(s) defines Exportation simply as 'the act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory.'

level3.question: How does 'Reexportation' under Section 102(jj) relate to 'Exportation' under Section 102(s)?

choices.A: Reexportation is unrelated to Exportation
choices.B: Reexportation is a form of Exportation specifically involving goods that have previously been imported
choices.C: Exportation only applies to reexported goods
choices.D: Reexportation applies only to relief consignments

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(jj) states that 'Reexportation means exportation of goods which have been imported,' making it a specific subset of the broader Exportation concept defined in Section 102(s). This layered definition is a common CuBLE terminology trap.

level4.question: A local manufacturer at the Bataan Freeport ships finished goods, made from domestic raw materials, out of the Philippines for sale abroad for the first time. What CMTA term applies?

choices.A: Reexportation
choices.B: Exportation
choices.D: Admission

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Since Section 102(s) defines Exportation as 'the act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory,' and these are domestically made goods leaving the country for the first time, not previously imported, this is Exportation rather than Reexportation.

level5.question: What CMTA term refers to the act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Exportation. Section 102(s) of the CMTA defines it as 'the act, documentation, and process of bringing goods out of Philippine territory.'

level1.question: Ilang porsyento ang maximum na protective tariff rate na maaaring itakda sa ilalim ng Flexible Clause?
level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(u), sa ilalim ng Flexible Clause, ang Pangulo ay may kapangyarihang baguhin ang tariff rates ngunit 'in no case shall be higher than one hundred percent (100%) ad valorem.' Ito ay isa sa pinaka madalas itanong na numero sa CuBLE.

level2.question: Under Section 102(u), the Flexible Clause grants the President the power to impose additional duty on all imports not exceeding:

choices.A: 5% ad valorem
choices.B: 10% ad valorem
choices.D: 20% ad valorem

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(u) provides that the President may 'impose additional duty on all import not exceeding ten percent (10%) ad valorem, whenever necessary.' This is a distinct cap from the 100% ceiling on protective tariff rate adjustments.

level3.question: Which government body must recommend the exercise of the President's Flexible Clause powers under Section 102(u)?

choices.A: Bureau of Customs
choices.B: National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)
choices.D: Department of Trade and Industry

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(u) states the Flexible Clause is exercised by 'the power of the President upon recommendation of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA).' Confusing NEDA's recommending role with the Tariff Commission is a common board exam trap.

level4.question: The President, acting on NEDA's recommendation, raises the tariff rate on a specific imported commodity from 60% to 95% ad valorem to protect a local industry. Is this action valid under the Flexible Clause?

choices.A: No, because any increase above 50% is prohibited
choices.B: Yes, because it does not exceed the 100% ad valorem ceiling under Section 102(u)
choices.C: No, because only Congress can adjust tariff rates
choices.D: Yes, but only if NEDA's recommendation is bypassed

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(u) allows the President, upon NEDA's recommendation, to increase protective tariff rates 'but in no case shall be higher than one hundred percent (100%) ad valorem.' Since 95% does not exceed this ceiling, the action is valid.

level5.question: Under Section 102(u) of the CMTA, what is the maximum ad valorem rate the President may set when increasing existing protective tariff rates under the Flexible Clause?
level5.reason: Correct answer: 100% ad valorem. Section 102(u) states the President's power to adjust protective tariff rates is limited such that the rate 'in no case shall be higher than one hundred percent (100%) ad valorem.' This is distinct from the separate 10% ad valorem ceiling on additional duties under the same clause.

level1.question: Magkano ang de minimis value kung saan walang duties at taxes na sisingilin sa goods, ayon sa Section 423?

choices.A: P10,000 pababa
choices.B: P5,000 pababa
choices.D: P100,000 pababa

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 423, 'No duties and taxes shall be collected on goods with an FOB or FCA value of ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) or below.' Huwag itong ikumpara sa P50,000 na threshold ng informal entry dahil magkaiba ang dalawang probisyon.

level2.question: Under Section 423, no duties and taxes shall be collected on goods with an FOB or FCA value of:

choices.A: P50,000 or below
choices.B: P100,000 or below
choices.D: P10,000 or below

level2.reason: Correct answer: D. Section 423 states that 'No duties and taxes shall be collected on goods with an FOB or FCA value of ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) or below.' This de minimis threshold is distinct from the P50,000 threshold for informal entry under Section 402.

level3.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the Free Zones enumerated under Section 102(w) of the CMTA?

choices.A: Clark Freeport Zone
choices.B: Cagayan Special Economic Zone and Freeport
choices.D: Freeport Area of Bataan

Section 102(w) enumerates specific chartered zones such as the Clark Freeport Zone, the Cagayan Special Economic Zone and Freeport under Republic Act No. 7922, and the Freeport Area of Bataan under Republic Act No. 9728, but the Makati Central Business District is not a legislated free zone under this list.

level4.question: A company operating within the Freeport Area of Bataan brings in imported machinery for its factory. Under the CMTA, how is this area classified?

choices.A: Customs territory
choices.B: Free Zone
choices.D: Bonded warehouse only

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(w) explicitly lists 'the Freeport Area of Bataan under Republic Act No. 9728' as one of the Free Zones under the CMTA. Goods moving into this area are subject to Admission rather than ordinary Entry.

level5.question: Under what Republic Act are PEZA-registered special economic zones established, as referenced in the CMTA's definition of Free Zone?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Republic Act No. 7916. Section 102(w) of the CMTA defines Free Zone to include 'special economic zones registered with the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) under Republic Act No. 7916, as amended.'

level1.question: Ano ang Goods ayon sa Section 102(x) ng CMTA?

choices.A: Articles, wares, merchandise at anumang item na subject ng importation o exportation
choices.B: Mga dokumento lamang
choices.D: Mga empleyado ng Bureau of Customs

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 102(x), ang Goods ay tumutukoy sa 'articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation.' Malawak ang saklaw ng terminong ito.

level2.question: Under Section 102(x), 'Goods' refers to:

choices.A: Only agricultural products
choices.B: Articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation
choices.C: Only luxury items subject to high tariffs
choices.D: Documents accompanying a shipment

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(x) broadly defines Goods as 'articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation.'

level3.question: Why is the CMTA's definition of 'Goods' under Section 102(x) considered broad rather than restrictive?

choices.A: It limits coverage to a specific list of commodities
choices.B: It uses general terms like 'articles, wares, merchandise and any other items' without limiting to specific categories
choices.D: It applies only to goods valued above a certain threshold

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(x) defines Goods using open-ended language covering 'articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation,' avoiding a restrictive or exhaustive list. This broad scope ensures the CMTA applies to virtually all tradable items unless specifically excluded elsewhere.

level4.question: A shipment arriving at the Port of Batangas includes machinery parts, raw materials, and packaging supplies, all intended for sale. Under Section 102(x), how are these items classified?

choices.A: They are not covered by the CMTA since they are mixed items
choices.B: They qualify as 'Goods' since they are articles, wares, or merchandise subject of importation
choices.C: Only the machinery qualifies as Goods
choices.D: Only items valued above a certain amount qualify as Goods

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Since Section 102(x) defines Goods broadly as 'articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation,' all the items in the shipment qualify as Goods under the CMTA.

level5.question: What CMTA term broadly covers articles, wares, merchandise, and any other items subject to importation or exportation?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Goods. Section 102(x) of the CMTA defines the term as 'articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation.'

level1.question: Kailan itinuturing na 'tentative' ang assessment ayon kay Section 425?

choices.A: Kapag hindi pa nabayaran ang duties
choices.B: Kapag hindi pa dumarating ang goods
choices.C: Kapag walang goods declaration na naihain
choices.D: Kapag dinidispute ng importer ang unang assessment ng duties at taxes

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: D. Ayon sa Section 425, 'Assessment shall be deemed tentative if the duties and taxes initially assessed are disputed by the importer.' Makukumpleto lang ang assessment kapag naresolba na ang tariff ruling o ang protest case.

level2.question: Under Section 425, an assessment is deemed tentative when:

choices.A: The goods declaration is incomplete
choices.B: The duties and taxes initially assessed are disputed by the importer
choices.C: The importer has not paid any duties
choices.D: The goods have not yet arrived

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 425 provides that 'Assessment shall be deemed tentative if the duties and taxes initially assessed are disputed by the importer.' The assessment only becomes complete upon final resolution of the classification dispute or protest case.

level1.question: Ano ang Importation ayon sa CMTA?

choices.A: Ang pagdadala ng goods mula sa foreign territory papasok sa Philippine territory
choices.B: Ang pagbebenta ng goods sa palengke
choices.D: Ang pag-export ng goods

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 102(z), ang Importation ay 'the act of bringing in of goods from a foreign territory into Philippine territory, whether for consumption, warehousing, or admission.' Kasama rito ang layuning consumption, warehousing, o admission sa free zone.

level2.question: Under Section 102(z), Importation may be for the purpose of consumption, warehousing, or:

choices.A: Reexportation only
choices.B: Admission
choices.D: Perishable storage only

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(z) states that Importation refers to bringing goods into Philippine territory, 'whether for consumption, warehousing, or admission as defined in this Act.' This links the Importation definition directly to the concept of Admission into a free zone.

level3.question: When does Importation, as defined in Section 102(z) and further explained in Section 103, legally begin?

choices.A: When the goods declaration is lodged
choices.B: When the carrying vessel or aircraft enters the Philippine territory with the intention to unload therein
choices.C: When duties and taxes are paid
choices.D: When the goods are physically unloaded at the port

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. While Section 102(z) defines Importation as the act of bringing goods into Philippine territory, Section 103 clarifies that 'Importation begins when the carrying vessel or aircraft enters the Philippine territory with the intention to unload therein.' Combining these two provisions is a common analytical question in CuBLE.

level4.question: A cargo ship carrying industrial equipment enters Philippine waters with clear intent to unload its cargo at the Port of Manila. At what point, under Section 103, is this importation considered to have begun?

choices.A: When the ship departs its foreign port of origin
choices.B: When the ship enters Philippine territory with the intention to unload
choices.C: When the goods are cleared by customs
choices.D: When duties and taxes are fully paid

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 103 states that 'Importation begins when the carrying vessel or aircraft enters the Philippine territory with the intention to unload therein,' making the entry into Philippine territory with unloading intent the legal starting point.

level5.question: What CMTA term refers to the act of bringing goods from a foreign territory into Philippine territory for consumption, warehousing, or admission?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Importation. Section 102(z) of the CMTA defines it as 'the act of bringing in of goods from a foreign territory into Philippine territory, whether for consumption, warehousing, or admission as defined in this Act.'

level1.question: Ano ang Lodgement ayon sa CMTA?

choices.A: Ang registration ng goods declaration sa Bureau
choices.B: Ang pagbabayad ng duties
choices.D: Ang pag-export ng goods

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 102(dd), ang Lodgement ay 'the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau.' Simple ngunit importante itong depinisyon dahil ginagamit ito sa buong proseso ng importation.

level2.question: Under Section 102(dd), 'Lodgement' refers to:

choices.A: The physical delivery of goods to a warehouse
choices.B: The registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau
choices.C: The payment of duties and taxes
choices.D: The appeal of a Bureau decision

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(dd) defines Lodgement simply as 'the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau.'

level3.question: Under Section 115, when are imported goods deemed 'entered' in the Philippines for consumption?

choices.A: When the goods physically arrive at the port
choices.B: When the goods declaration is electronically lodged, together with any required supporting documents, with the pertinent customs office
choices.C: When duties and taxes are fully paid
choices.D: When the importer signs a commercial invoice

level3.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 115 states that imported goods 'shall be deemed "entered" in the Philippines for consumption when the goods declaration is electronically lodged, together with any required supporting documents, with the pertinent customs office.' This ties the Lodgement definition to the legal moment of Entry for consumption purposes.

level4.question: An importer at the Port of Cebu electronically submits a complete goods declaration with all required supporting documents to the customs office. What CMTA term describes this act?

choices.A: Assessment
choices.B: Lodgement
choices.D: Admission

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(dd) defines Lodgement as 'the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau,' which matches the act of electronically submitting the declaration to the customs office.

level5.question: What CMTA term refers to the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Lodgement. Section 102(dd) of the CMTA defines it as 'the registration of a goods declaration with the Bureau.'

level1.question: Ano ang Outright Smuggling?

choices.A: Pag-import ng goods na may kumpletong dokumento
choices.B: Pag-import ng goods nang walang complete customs documents o hindi cleared, para makaiwas sa pagbabayad ng buwis
choices.D: Pag-export ng goods papunta sa ibang bansa

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 102(ff), ang Outright Smuggling ay ang pag-import 'without complete customs prescribed importation documents, or without being cleared by customs or other regulatory government agencies, for the purpose of evading payment of prescribed taxes, duties and other government charges.' Iba ito sa Technical Smuggling na may dokumento pero peke o mali.

level2.question: Under Section 102(ff), Outright Smuggling involves importing goods:

choices.A: With falsified declarations as to quality or quantity
choices.B: Without complete customs prescribed importation documents, or without being cleared by customs, to evade taxes and duties
choices.C: With proper clearance but incorrect valuation
choices.D: Through legitimate ports with full documentation

level2.reason: Correct answer: B. Section 102(ff) defines Outright Smuggling as importing goods 'without complete customs prescribed importation documents, or without being cleared by customs or other regulatory government agencies, for the purpose of evading payment of prescribed taxes, duties and other government charges.'

level3.question: What is the key distinction between Outright Smuggling and Technical Smuggling under the CMTA?

choices.A: Outright Smuggling involves goods imported without complete documents or clearance, while Technical Smuggling involves fraudulent or erroneous declarations of goods already documented
choices.B: Outright Smuggling applies only to exports, while Technical Smuggling applies only to imports
choices.C: Technical Smuggling requires no documentation at all
choices.D: There is no meaningful difference between the two terms

level3.reason: Correct answer: A. Section 102(ff) defines Outright Smuggling as importing goods without complete documents or clearance, while Section 102(pp) defines Technical Smuggling as importing 'by means of fraudulent, falsified or erroneous declaration of the goods to its nature, kind, quality, quantity or weight.' This distinction is one of the most frequently tested comparisons in CuBLE.

level4.question: A cargo container arrives at the Port of Manila with no import documents filed at all, bypassing customs clearance entirely to avoid paying duties. What type of smuggling is this?

choices.A: Technical Smuggling
choices.B: Outright Smuggling
choices.D: Tentative Release violation

level4.reason: Correct answer: B. Since the goods entered 'without complete customs prescribed importation documents, or without being cleared by customs,' this matches the Section 102(ff) definition of Outright Smuggling, as distinguished from Technical Smuggling, which involves falsified declarations of properly documented goods.

level5.question: What CMTA term describes importing goods without complete customs documents or clearance for the purpose of evading duties and taxes?
level5.reason: Correct answer: Outright Smuggling. Section 102(ff) of the CMTA defines it as importing goods 'without complete customs prescribed importation documents, or without being cleared by customs or other regulatory government agencies, for the purpose of evading payment of prescribed taxes, duties and other government charges.'

level1.question: Kailan itinuturing na final ang assessment ayon kay Section 429?

choices.C: Kaagad pagkatapos ng lodgement ng goods declaration
choices.D: 1 taon pagkatapos ng payment

level1.reason: Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 429, 'Assessment shall be deemed final fifteen (15) days after receipt of the notice of assessment by the importer or consignee.' Dito nagsisimula ang bilang ng panahon para maghain ng protesta kung sakaling dinidispute ang assessment.

level2.question: Under Section 429, an assessment becomes final:

choices.A: Upon lodgement of the goods declaration
choices.B: 30 days after release of goods
choices.C: 15 days after receipt of the notice of assessment by the importer or consignee
choices.D: Immediately upon examination

235._title: Title IV – Import Clearance and Formalities

level1.question: Ilang taon mula sa final payment ng duties at taxes bago maging conclusive ang assessment, kung walang fraud, ayon sa Section 430?

level2.question: Under Section 430, in the absence of fraud, the assessment becomes conclusive upon all parties how many years from the date of final payment of duties and taxes?

choices.A: 1 year
choices.B: 5 years
choices.D: 3 years

level2.reason: Correct answer: D. Section 430 provides that, absent fraud, 'the assessment shall be conclusive upon all parties three (3) years from the date of final payment of duties and taxes, or upon completion of the post clearance audit.' This period of limitation does not apply in cases involving fraud.

level1.question: Ayon sa Section 431, maaaring i-release ng Bureau ang goods kahit hindi pa alam ang resulta ng laboratory analysis, basta't may naipost na sapat na security. Tama o Mali?

choices.A: Cannot be Determined
choices.B: True
choices.D: Partially True

level2.question: Under Section 431, when the Bureau requires laboratory analysis of samples before release, the goods may still be released:

choices.A: Only after the analysis results are known
choices.B: Never, until results are known
choices.C: After posting of sufficient security by the declarant
choices.D: Only with the Commissioner's personal approval
